Page 2.
1947, November 7
V. Sister Mary Cecilia. Mount Saint Joseph, Chio.
After that he drove down every week for several months. Febr.29th - I believe he had the whole Family down - having enrolled some other, as he nearly always did, he concluded about as follows: "Now Father; I want to enroll the Poor Souls as I promised them I would. Put them down for a good half of that $25. - fourteen dollars."
Some years afterwards I was up to see an old lady in Smith's Creek who died shortly after with cancer of the stomach and your Father having heard of my visit came and took me over to see the little farm you refer to and I remember seeing little Dorothy. Congratulations on my "dream" even then of her vocation. Try at least to become appreciative for such a really surpassing privilege. - Think of it Sister M.C. . A chosen spouse from among millions, - a spouse of the eternal King/kings! How little it is possible for any mere creature to be adequately grateful for such a privileged calling! We can only try and that suffices. Do not forget to send in the name of your little "hopeless case" friend, and to have as many as possible to offer prayers and holy Communions, not only for her but for so many more sadly unfortunate "big shots" in hospitals and elsewhere who, having little or no faith, in the super- natural, refuse to believe in even the possibility of miracles, and who by a manifest miracle might be induced to at least pray for the gift of faith -- which Almighty God is only waiting to be asked for. Sincerely yours in Christ,
Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.
